output.name: Hulun
output.myth: When the snow lets go of the cliffs, the goats go mad with spring and want every ledge at once. Hesk, who keeps count, showed the herders how to lift a crook and turn the flock uphill, where the wind keeps the grass short and the rot cannot follow. That crook is Hulun. Its hook hangs in the north over the gull-road, and its foot is the bright stone at the bottom of the sky. Ennu carved the shaft from a goat's shin, which the goat has not forgiven. When Aun cut the string he took one nanny up by mistake, and she is still up there, working the Lamp Road for good grass. East of her the Name-Kite flies its knots at midsummer, when the light stays late, and Kessal the Mooring Post keeps watch from the north-west over her kelp pool, where the ebb never quite lets go. Orrun does not say whether the sea needs turning too. Go up after her, the old women say, and keep your count.
output.finding: Find the Name-Kite on the Lamp Road, and Hulun lies about a fist (11°) to its west, with its hook over the gull-road to the north.
